subject: english-literature
title: Iago and the Architecture of Jealousy
welcome_lead: Shakespeare's 1603 tragedy maps jealousy from whisper to murder. Examine Iago's design.
meta_desc: A-Level Othello — Iago's manipulation, jealousy and tragic structure.
final_note: You have followed Iago's blueprint — and seen how the play's tragedy is engineered.

concepts.def: Poetics: tragic hero's error or flaw causes downfall; Othello's jealousy, Macbeth's ambition, Lear's pride.
Purgation of pity and fear in audience; tragedy's moral function; debated by AC Bradley (1904).
Moor of Venice manipulated by Iago into killing Desdemona; race, jealousy, manipulation; tragic Othello restores honour.
Aged king divides kingdom by daughters' flattery; Cordelia banished, Goneril and Regan turn; tragic recognition of madness.
Shakespearean Tragedy; character-based criticism; tragic hero exceptional but flawed; lasting influence.

concepts.term: G. Wilson Knight Wheel of Fire 1930
concepts.def: Spatial pattern criticism; opposes Bradley's character focus; reads symbolic structures and imagery.

walkthroughs.body_html: Act I establishes status; Act II isolates the cast on Cyprus; Act III stages the temptation scene where jealousy is planted; Act IV sees Othello's collapse; Act V the murder and Iago's exposure.

Coleridge described Iago's motiveless malignity — the gap between his stated reasons (promotion grievance, suspicion of Emilia) and the scale of his evil.

Modern critics often re-anchor Iago in race, class or military hierarchy to fill that gap.
Iago's masterstroke in III.iii is to name what he is fostering: O, beware, my lord, of jealousy; / It is the green-eyed monster. Naming it implants it.
